answer: Every new identity must serve a turn as harbour jury: it is moored to a jetty of real disputes, handed one case per epoch by lottery, and must write a signed verdict before the epoch's gale closes. Each verdict is checked against the majority; a wrong call forfeits the identity's bond and drops it from the ledge of trust, while a right call slowly builds standing. A clone farm must staff a hundred separate jury seats, read a hundred different cases, and risk a hundred bonds — work no fake can copy, because every case and signature belongs to one identity alone.
